note: General IPM guidance only. No pesticide brand/dose is prescribed here; entries cite org-level sources (IRRI/CABI/APS/ICAR). If a disease has no entry, the API must say verified guidance is unavailable rather than inventing treatment.

management: Remove and destroy infected debris; avoid leaving infected stubble in the field.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization during humid periods.
Improve air circulation with recommended spacing and drainage.
Consult a local extension officer for currently registered fungicide options in your state.
prevention: Prefer resistant varieties recommended for your region by the state agricultural university.
Use clean seed and treat seed as per local extension guidance.
Practice rotation and monitor the crop weekly in humid weather.
symptoms: Diamond-shaped leaf lesions with gray centers and dark borders.
Neck infection can cause panicles to break.
Infected nodes may turn dark and rot.
entries.title: Rice blast — general guidance

management: Remove affected lower leaves and destroy them away from the field.
Mulch to reduce soil splash onto leaves.
Prefer drip irrigation over overhead watering.
Consult a local extension officer for currently registered options.
prevention: Practice rotation (avoid solanaceous crops in the same plot).
symptoms: Dark spots with concentric rings on older leaves.
Yellowing and defoliation starting from lower leaves.
entries.title: Tomato early blight — general guidance

management: Destroy infected foliage away from the field; do not compost infected material.
Seek extension advice quickly — late blight spreads fast in cool wet weather.
prevention: Monitor closely during cool, wet periods.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions turning brown with pale margins.
White mold growth under leaves in humid conditions.
entries.title: Tomato late blight — general guidance

management: Destroy infected crop residue after harvest.
Follow extension guidance on seed treatment and registered options.
prevention: Use certified seed of recommended varieties.
Rotate crops and manage volunteer plants.
symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots turning brown.
Black streaks on stems; boll rot in severe cases.
entries.title: Cotton bacterial blight — general guidance

management: Remove and destroy infected plants to reduce virus source.
Manage the whitefly vector (yellow sticky traps, weed-free field) per extension guidance.
prevention: Avoid growing near other virus hosts; use barrier crops where advised.
symptoms: Upward/downward leaf curl with thickened veins.
Stunted growth and reduced fruit set.
entries.title: Chilli leaf curl — general guidance

management: Remove badly affected leaves and maintain field sanitation.
symptoms: Leaf spots that enlarge and dry; severe cases defoliate plants.
entries.title: Turmeric leaf spot — general guidance
